references.title: ISPOR — The Professional Society for Health Economics and Outcomes Research

title: AI Market Access & Pricing Intelligence Assistant
short: Organizes pricing references, reimbursement rules and health-economic evidence to prepare market access dossiers faster.
symptom: Pricing and reimbursement files take months to prepare
ingredient: An evidence organizer for market access teams
directions: Choose the product and target market. Get a structured evidence pack: comparators, reference prices, budget-impact inputs and evidence gaps.
problem: Market access teams must collect clinical and economic evidence, comparator prices, reference-pricing rules and payer requirements for each country, often from scratch.
why: Slow or weak dossiers delay patient access and reduce the chance of listing at a sustainable price.
solution: Retrieves and organizes published clinical and economic evidence, tracks comparator and reference prices from public sources, structures budget-impact inputs and highlights evidence gaps for the health-economics team.
data: Public price lists and reimbursement rules
limitations: Health-economic models must be built and validated by experts
Pricing rules differ and change by country
review: Health economists and market access managers build the models and sign off every submission.
